provenance.note: Status changes only with a dated citation; per-commitment citations inline (commitment_source + status_history entries). update_model names the verification calendar: DPCC monthly Yamuna report for river/drain outcomes, the Economic Survey and DJB budget for spending claims, the June Flood Control Order, Chhath season, and CAG follow-ups - which is why those registry entries carry this file in dependsOn.

payload.headline: The Yamuna promise stack: Delhi's dated commitments
payload.intro: Delhi's water governance runs on announced deadlines - drains to be trapped by a date, treatment capacity by a year, a river 'clean' within three years. This register keeps each commitment with its original citation and never overwrites a date: when a deadline moves or passes silently, that history is the finding.

status_legend.delivered: Done, with a source confirming it
status_legend.slipped: Officially or credibly re-dated - the old and new dates are both kept
status_legend.overdue: Past its promised date with no official word
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

commitments.title: Trap all 39 major drains outfalling to the Yamuna
commitments.committed_by: Delhi government (I&FC / DJB, Yamuna rejuvenation programme)
commitments.what: March 2026 reporting: 17 drains already trapped, work underway on 22 more, with the government's stated target of completing the trapping by 30 June 2026. Drain-trapping is the load-bearing claim in every Yamuna clean-up plan - untrapped drains are how 84% of the pollution load reaches the river.

commitment_source.label: Amar Ujala, 24 March 2026 - '17 drains trapped, work underway on 22 others' with the 30 June target

status_history.note: 17 of 39 trapped; 22 in progress against the 30 June 2026 target

Deadline passed three weeks ago; no known public completion announcement or updated count as of this register's compilation. First DPCC monthly report covering July should show it in the drain-quality numbers if trapping completed.
status_history.source_label: Register compilation check (no citable update found)

status_history.note: Checked the Delhi government's latest monthly progress report to NMCG for the NGT (June 2026). It counts drains differently from this row: "There are 22 drains out falling into river Yamuna in Delhi out of which 10 Drains were tapped as informed by DJB and One drain (Abul Fazal Drain) is not to be tapped." It sets out an action plan for the remaining 11. The 30 June 2026 date has passed and we have not found a completion record for the 39 drains.
status_history.source_label: DPCC, Monthly Progress Report of Govt. of NCT of Delhi for June 2026 in NGT OA 673/2018 (covering letter dated 19 August 2026), on the NMCG portal

commitments.title: Mission Sahibi: dredge the silt-choked Najafgarh drain
commitments.what: A bathymetric survey found ~9.1 million cubic metres of silt on the bed of the 57-km drain. The mission deploys 32 machines including Finnish Watermaster amphibious dredgers to restore carrying capacity - both a pollution intervention and flood-season insurance for west Delhi.

commitment_source.label: ETV Bharat, March 2026 - Mission Sahibi launch, silt survey and equipment details

status_history.note: Launch reported with survey numbers and machine deployment

Checked for a progress figure. The newest dated report we found is department-wide: officials said the Irrigation and Flood Control Department "has also completed 93 per cent of the desilting work across 77 drains, with more than 31 lakh metric tonnes (MT) of silt already removed", drains that include the Najafgarh drain. We have not found a Najafgarh-only figure against the survey estimate of about 9.1 million cubic metres, or a completion date for the mission.
status_history.source_label: ThePrint (PTI), reporting Delhi government officials and the Flood Control Minister, 3 July 2026

commitments.title: Rs 860 crore: 12 decentralised STPs along the Najafgarh drain
commitments.what: Approved project to intercept and treat sewage entering the Najafgarh drain - the channel carrying the largest single share of Delhi's Yamuna pollution load - through 12 decentralised treatment plants rather than trunk diversion.

commitment_source.label: ANI, 24 May 2026, reporting a Delhi government release: the Chief Minister's approval of 12 DSTPs in the Najafgarh region at about Rs 860 crore, 46.5 MGD combined

status_history.note: Approval reported; no known public tender/construction milestone yet. Needs a dated procurement citation to move to on-track.
status_history.source_label: ANI, reporting the Delhi Chief Minister through a government release, 24 May 2026 (approval of 12 DSTPs in the Najafgarh region at about Rs 860 crore)

status_history.note: MoHUA's AMRUT 2.0 weekly progress report lists "DJB-Construction of 7 Nos. of Decentralized Sewage Treatment Plant and Sewage Pumping Station along with other associated / allied appurtenant work on under Najafgarh drainage" at 2.00% physical progress, expenditure incurred Rs 0.00 crore, awarded cost Rs 387.00 crore. We have not confirmed which of the 12 approved sites this package covers, or found a progress record for the other plants, so the status is kept.
status_history.source_label: MoHUA, AMRUT 2.0 National Progress Comparison Report (current week 18-10-2026; the file is regenerated weekly)

commitments.title: Rs 403 crore STP upgrade package
commitments.what: 2025 package approved by DJB's board: upgrading the Yamuna Vihar Phase-III STP from 25 to 40 MGD and building a new 15 MGD STP at Yamuna Vihar Phase-IV, with 12 years of operation and maintenance, to meet the latest DPCC and NGT standards. It directly answers the NGT record (75% of STPs lacking disinfection; treated effluent from 25 of 35 STPs not meeting DPCC norms per the CAG).

commitment_source.label: india.com report on the Rs 403 crore Yamuna clean-up / STP upgrade plan

status_history.note: Sanction reported; per-plant scope and completion dates not yet public. Economic Survey and DJB budget documents are the verification venue.
status_history.source_label: india.com, 10 February 2026, report on the Rs 403 crore STP upgrade plan

status_history.note: DJB's statement on its 173rd board meeting, reported by The Patriot on 11 August 2025, described the Rs 403 crore project as upgrading the Yamuna Vihar Phase-III STP from 25 to 40 MGD and building a new 15 MGD STP at Phase-IV. The Delhi government's June 2026 progress report to NMCG lists Yamuna Vihar Phase-III (existing 25 MGD, enhanced capacity 15 MGD) among existing STPs to be upgraded, with the status "Tendering work is in process for Upgradation, Work to be awarded by: July, 2026" and a timeline of December 2027. We have not found an award or progress record, so the status is kept.
status_history.source_label: DPCC, Monthly Progress Report of Govt. of NCT of Delhi for June 2026 in NGT OA 673/2018 (covering letter dated 19 August 2026), on the NMCG portal, Annexure 2

commitments.title: Raise sewage-treatment capacity to 1,250 MGD by June 2027
commitments.what: The umbrella capacity target behind the STP packages (Rs 901 crore sanctioned for +51.5 MGD across 8 plants; 3 new STPs; 18 upgrades from 343 to 456 MGD). Context for scale: the CAG's audit-period baseline had 594 MGD generated and 545 MGD treated by 35 STPs, with 212.59 MGD from unauthorised colonies entering storm drains untreated.

commitment_source.label: ThePrint (PTI), 11 July 2025, quoting the Delhi Water Minister: "We plan to increase this to 1,250 MGD by June 2027"

status_history.note: Component sanctions (Rs 901 cr / Rs 860 cr / Rs 403 cr) are moving; no independent capacity audit yet against the headline number.
status_history.source_label: india.com, 10 February 2026, reporting the Rs 403 crore STP plan and DJB's 2025 sanction of Rs 901 crore for 51.5 MGD across eight STPs

status_history.note: The Delhi government's June 2026 progress report to NMCG for the NGT gives installed capacity as 814 MGD and the plan as "Total Capacity of STPs by December, 2027 876 MGD" and "Total Capacity of STPs by January, 2028 1506 MGD". On that schedule capacity is 876 MGD in December 2027, below 1,250 MGD, and passes 1,250 MGD only with the January 2028 step, so the revised date is January 2028. Separately, the Water Minister said on 29 July 2026 (PTI): "The target is to ultimately have 1,041 MGD of sewage treatment capacity after completion of all approved projects", with DJB planning to complete the projects by 2028.
status_history.source_label: DPCC, Monthly Progress Report of Govt. of NCT of Delhi for June 2026 in NGT OA 673/2018 (covering letter dated 19 August 2026), on the NMCG portal

commitments.title: A 'clean Yamuna' within the government's stated three-year horizon
commitments.committed_by: Delhi government (2025 administration), echoing the central Yamuna push
commitments.what: The political umbrella over every entry above. At Yamunotsav 2025 the Delhi Water Minister said the government has set a target of revitalising the Yamuna in three years, citing progress over the previous eight months. We have not found an official statement that sets a bathing standard or ties the target to Chhath. This register treats it as the accountability wrapper: its verifiable content is the DPCC monthly numbers at the 8 river stations and 27 drains.

commitment_source.label: Devdiscourse (PTI), 3 November 2025, reporting the Delhi Water Minister at Yamunotsav 2025 on the government's target of revitalising the Yamuna "in just three years"

status_history.note: Programme components funded and moving; the DPCC monthly series (faecal coliform + BOD at ITO/Nizamuddin/Okhla) is the scoreboard this register will cite. The 2025 Chhath froth season is the first hard checkpoint.
status_history.source_label: DPCC monthly analysis reports (river Yamuna, drains, STPs), the series this entry names as the scoreboard

status_history.note: Re-based on the Water Minister's statement at Yamunotsav 2025. PTI reported, citing the minister: "The Delhi government has set the ambitious target of revitalizing the Yamuna River in just three years". The statement gives no date and no measure of a clean river. We have not found an official statement setting a bathing standard or a Chhath date, so the earlier due date of 30 November 2027 is removed and the current status cannot be assessed either way.
status_history.source_label: Devdiscourse (PTI), 3 November 2025, reporting the Delhi Water Minister at Yamunotsav 2025

commitments.title: Renuka, Lakhwar and Kishau dams - the perpetual augmentation promise
commitments.committed_by: Government of India + basin states (Delhi co-funding Renuka's water component)
commitments.what: Three upper-Yamuna storage dams promised for decades as the fix for Delhi's raw-water ceiling. Delhi's own auditor has now rendered the register's verdict for it: CAG Report No. 3 of 2025 calls the prospects of augmentation from these projects 'remote'.

commitment_source.label: CAG Report No. 3 of 2025 ('augmentation remote' finding; tabled 23 March 2026)

status_history.note: Apex-audit verdict: 'remote'. Kept open because the promise keeps being re-announced.

commitments.title: Wazirabad WTP and command-area rehabilitation (post-ADB withdrawal)
commitments.what: The CAG found that planning failures led ADB to withdraw Rs 2,243 crore of financing for the Wazirabad WTP rehabilitation under the Delhi Water Supply Improvement Investment Programme, and delayed the Chandrawal rehabilitation. The rehabilitation itself remains necessary; this entry tracks what replaces the withdrawn financing.

commitment_source.label: CAG Report No. 3 of 2025, Chapter 5 (projects and works execution)

status_history.note: Financing withdrawn per the audit; no known public replacement plan yet

payload.update_model: Statuses change only with a dated citation; every change appends to the commitment's history - the slippage trail is the product. Delhi's verification calendar: DPCC monthly Yamuna report (~25th of each month) for river/drain outcomes; the Economic Survey (Feb-Mar) and DJB budget for spending claims; the monsoon Flood Control Order (June) for drain works; the Chhath season (Oct-Nov) as the annual public checkpoint on the river itself; CAG follow-ups as they table.
payload.sources_note: Several cited news pages (ThePrint, india.com, Amar Ujala) block automated fetchers but open normally in a browser; the CAG PDFs and government pages were verified directly on 2026-07-20.
